correctness.rationale: Correct as written for the normalized zeroth-Hermite Gaussian eigenvalue, not the full localization norm. Exact digit integration gives lambda0=(1-e^{-h}) product_{j=1}^n(1+e^{-2A/3^j}), h=A/3^n. Splitting at floor(log_3 A) and comparing convergent product tails yields the claimed 3-periodic multiplier H(t)=t^delta K(t), delta=log_3 2, and exp(±eta) relative bound for A>=1, A<3^n. The bilateral log-derivative series has the eight-term lower partial sum 0.6315473360799694 > delta 0.6309297535714574, so nonconstant. Re-read exact rational Taylor majorants in source CHECK.py and the reported 62 test assertions. Finite tests do not replace the infinite convergence/tail proof.

originality.rationale: FAIL: substantial prior mathematical implication, not just similar vocabulary. Grabner–Prodinger, Asymptotic Analysis of the Moments of the Cantor Distribution (1996), pp. 2-5, explicitly gives the Laplace transform B(z)=product_{k>=0}(1+exp[-(1-theta)theta^k z])/2, its z^{-log_{1/theta}2} times nonconstant log-periodic Fourier profile with sharp expansion; choose theta=1/3. This B(A) is exactly the infinite Cantor product (indices shifted) underlying H(A): for A=t*3^m, 2^m B(A) -> K(t), hence A^delta B(A)->H(t), so the prior F(log_3 A) equals this H(A). The 2020 Knutsen article already prints the finite-n Gaussian eigenvalue product; its elementary truncation plus prior B(A) yields the finite explicit error estimate. The claim is covered in substance even though the exact bound eta is not printed verbatim in the 1996 paper.
